Ethiopia

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Whilst the figures remain unclear due to informal travel means, it's believed that thousands of Ethiopians call South Africa home. Many work in the informal retail sector in the city centre or in townships. The insert will tell the story of the ongoing war through some colorful characters, that left home because of war and economic strife, and follow the on going events on the news, social media and communications with relatives. Expert analysis will recount Ethiopia's history, recent economic developments and the prospects of this country's future

Summary:
It's been a year since Ethiopia has been engaged in a war that has killed thousands and left millions displaced. This internal conflict erupted in the northern, Tigray region, where the TPLF attacked the Ethiopian army in attempt to establish the province as an independent state. The ongoing conflict has caused a humanitarian crisis, particularly in the north, with aid groups criticising the government for blocking aid, food and the supplies from reaching the region. With growing global criticism and futile attempts at mediation by the African Union, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has found himself isolated in the international community. The United States recently kicked Ethiopia from AGOA, a trading pact between America and African countries that allows for favourable agreements.

Human rights groups as well the United Nations has highlighted extreme human rights abuses, from both the TPLF and the government. Amnesty International's report from a recent research trip there, found that rape and sexual abuse, was being used as a weapon of war.

Ethiopia has registered double digit growth over the past ten years and after Abiy Ahmed took office, there was greater opportunity of growth. He had a clear vision to develop the country, with investors in banking and ICT sectors really keen to set up shop in one of the fastest growing economies in the region.

After receiving the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019, there was greater social buy-in into Ahmed's leadership and vision, many expats who'd left their home country decades ago, were looking forward to returning home and rebuild the country. Ahmed appointed the country's first woman president, garnering more support as a new age African leader.

01;04 kassa –there was a bit of a mess in the country and most of us wanted to go out and stop the fight from outside. Instead of doing it from inside and shedding blood. We didn’t want to shed blood, we just want to have proper democratic elected government and eh so I ended up getting a visa straight to johannesburg. 01;58 I wasn’t supposed to stay actually, I was supposed to be in the u.s and eh join the rest of my family then someone took me to Soweto, big mistake. I fell in love with Soweto


Soweto and all its attractions, are 5000km away from this man’s home country, where people he still holds dear, face an uncertain and violent future; the very thing that drove him and 1000s of his countrymen and women from their homeland in the first place.


Kassahaun Gebrehana or Kassa, to his patrons runs one of Johannesburg's much loved Ethiopian restaurants. Little Addis, is an ode to his late mother, who was a chef and kept the family recipes. Kassa left his hometown, Addis Ababa 20 years ago.


Sit Down Interview - Kassa
00;58 Kassa – remember it’s end of 1999 and the beginning od 2000s and there was a war between Eritrea and Ethiopia at that time and to tell you the truth I didn’t want to be in that war. I don’t want to be in any conflict, we just came out of civil war and we were doing a okay then all of a sudden we are fighting our brothers but now they are independent. My entire family was against war. And we just said, you guys sort it out and lets move. And we start talking and we start telling that war, what we see we don’t like. You know the civil war was all about power grabbing mechanism and on top of that you are dividing up the cuontr, ethnic based federalism. And they were looking for us, we became trouble makers. 02;19 so when I got a chance to leave, I took it and I came to south Africa.

Kassa’s home country Ethiopia is beset by war, once again. The east african nation has a long history conflict, strife and struggle.

2018 saw the end of a protracted fight between Ethiopia and neighbouring Eritrea, the peace talks were led by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.

The country enjoyed stability, development and economic progress.

For political economist Siyaduma Biniza, this was historic milestone

Siya
04;06 Siya – definitely, and also being a young or among the young or the youngest actually presidents on the continent, I think at 44 or 45 years old he also represented a sort of revival, an economic revival of Ethiopia and attracted a lot of investment.
04;52 And hence I think that turning point, that mildstone in the country also attracted a lot of Ethiopians who were around the world, the diaspora, to come back to Ethiopia, to reinvest in Ethiopia


Then in November 2020, conflict erupted in the northern Tigray Region.

The Tigray People’s Liberation Front, which ruled Ethiopia for 27 years before losing power, has re-emerged and is on a campaign of self determination, fighting to break away as an independent country in the province where it is the ethnic majority.

(INTRO SAMUEL)


Samuel
1806 – looking back on the era of the TPLF, 27 years, before abiy came into power, prime minister abiy. They led a coalition government that was really led by them, why they get credit for changing Ethiopia in terms of building infrastructure and so on. But in terms of human rights we really had issues, Ethiopians had issues, they really abused the rights of Ethiopians. They denied democracy



In a move to assert itself against the state, the TPLF attacked an Ethiopian government army base in Tigray. The federal government retaliated with force and fire, and to stamp its authority, branded the Tigray’s People’s Liberation Front a terrorist group.

Siya

14;26 actually the TPLF is the strongest military force in Ethiopia currently, 14;55 and so when Eritrea broke away that left the tplf has the strongest military force currently in Ethiopia. So the contradiction lies now in that the federal government should have control of the entire Ethiopia, the entire geographical region. But the problem is that is the control and power of the federal government is contested by a strong military force that is making military progress on its own right and is reaching its military mildstones, is a power check.


It’s a display of military power for the TPLF and a quest to establish its authority for the Ethiopian government.

This battle has left thousands killed and millions displaced.
And the reports of ethnic massacres and deliberate murders of young men, leave Kasa deeply shaken.





Kassa
11:53 Unless you want to take it back to where we used to be, why do you have to do that, why do you have to kill innocent people. Why do you have to shed blood,


Professor Mamo Muchie, talks to relatives back home on a daily basis. He too says this conflict is reminiscent of past wars

Muchie

10:51 - 11;11 why is this people want to continue again to rule and if they were not able to rule, why do they want to go to war. Why do they want to kill children, why do they want to use children as soldiers. Children should go to school we should give them books’

It’s been a year since the conflict erupted, with human rights organisations reporting mass civilian killings and sexual violence meted out against women and girls. With no sign of peaceful dialogue between the Ethiopian government and the TPLF, there is growing concern that innocent people will continue to suffer.



In its report, human rights organisation Amnesty International, categorised the scale and gravity of sexual violations in this conflict as crimes against humanity. Donatella Roverra, Senior Crisis Response Advisor says women and girls have endured the worst atrocities

Donatella
03;33 The range of human rights violations we’ve documented it includes large scale civilian killings, deliberate killing of civilians, massacres, extr-judicial torture of civilians who have been captured. And then killed in extr-juduicial killings, rape, of women and girls by all forces. In the Tigray region, in the Amhara region, women as well as girls as young as 13, 14, rapes carried out by multiple perpatrators. 04;21 Women and girls held in conditions of sexual slavery for not just days but weeks but months.
Claire- what is the impact of this….

10;50 having surivived, been a victim of rape is great in Ethiopian society. And so I’ve interviewed women and girls who were married and who’s husbands have divorced them, have abandoned them because they do not want to be with them after what they have endured.


These are victims of war, cut off from the world, in remote towns and villages.

It makes Samuel’s of reporting these horrors challenging but all the more important

Samuel

10:50 So it has really affected people on the ground, if you stay in addis ababa and make a determination of where the country is headed, you’d think everything is okay, everything is fine. 11;13 but it’s only when you leave, when go outside addis ababa that you see the impact this conflict has on Ethiopians., that’s when you understand that conflict has too many victims and Ethiopia is no exception.


But the TPLF claims that it’s taking the fight to the capital.

Reports suggest the group is edging closer to Addis Ababa.

Anxious about this development, a state of emergency was announced and local authorities, called on citizens to register their guns for a fight on the frontlines.


Samuel
00;51 – there are too many rumours, we have been reading about, we have been seeing from afar, especially on social media. But Adis Ababa in the day time is as normal as it gets, the streets are busy. There are many activities we see in the open but when it gets dark the country is in a state of emergency, so there are more scrutiny, there are more government officials including the police asking for ID,

A state of emergency and a looming humanitarian crisis in the worst affected regions, the internal fighting in Ethiopia has threatened the economic development and progress made in the last few years.



This was one of the fastest expanding economies on the continent, registering double digit growth.
Coffee and tea, its staple exports were doing well, more tourists were visiting the country after the 2018 peace deal was brokered. Foreign investors were keenly eyeing the 100 million population market.


05;15 Siya – definitely, and it’s really flung Ethiopia back to the period of the 70s and 80s when it faced internal civil war and famine etc, currently the’re estimates of around 4 or 5 million Ethiopians who are living in famine like conditions as a result of the conflict, a lot of people are internally displaced running away from conflict ridden parts into neighbouring provinces in the southern parts but also neighbouring countries such as sudan and its really undone the progress the country has made since 2018.


Samuel

06:22 it has really really impacted the economy, there are many businesses that are going out of business. Many foreign investments are questioning the wisdom of staying in Ethiopia, and the conflict has suspended the transportation that used to bring goods to Ethiopia and to the capital and to other places. The price of even onion is going up, even from the richest person in Ethiopia, to the poorest, those that sell onion on the ground have been affected. So it’s been an overwhelming and expensive conflict. The Ethiopian government estimates that 07:08 they’ve spent so much money, even in the billions, the

Siya

25;03 Siya – definitely and it’s already been murked by the fact he responded militarily to an internal conflict. He was able to broker peace and negotiate peace with neighbouring Eritrea but the response to the Tigrayan problem was an immediate military response justified or not, given the fact that the tplf made an attack on the centra; government;s military installation. It is definitely about his legacy now, and it depends on whether going forward this is a long protracted conflict or whether they are able to reach a negoatiation settlement soon
Siya
03;19 and secondly what he came into power as advocating for, peace and security and also his impact in ending the ten year war between Ethiopia and Eritrea was very emphatic in sort of changing the perceptions of Ethiopia but also created huge hope that Ethiopia was now entering a new dawn. Unfortunately a couple of years later the country finds itself on the brink of civil war



With no indication of peace talks or negotiation, the conflict continues to gain momentum.

14;35 well both sides are saying they will fight in the end, fight until the end. And that’s what we’re watching, there are man people that are trying to solve it in a peaceful way and with two factors or two teams that are not willing to sit down and negotiate. I thin kit’s really difficult to really give you a sound bite kind of answer.

metadata.Summary: It's been a year since Ethiopia has been engaged in a war that has killed thousands and left millions displaced. This internal conflict erupted in the northern, Tigray region, where the TPLF attacked the Ethiopian army in attempt to establish the province as an independent state. The ongoing conflict has caused a humanitarian crisis, particularly in the north, with aid groups criticising the government for blocking aid, food and the supplies from reaching the region. With growing global criticism and futile attempts at mediation by the African Union, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has found himself isolated in the international community. The United States recently kicked Ethiopia from AGOA, a trading pact between America and African countries that allows for favourable agreements. Human rights groups as well the United Nations has highlighted extreme human rights abuses, from both the TPLF and the government. Amnesty International's report from a recent research trip there, found that rape and sexual abuse, was being used as a weapon of war. Ethiopia has registered double digit growth over the past ten years and after Abiy Ahmed took office, there was greater opportunity of growth. He had a clear vision to develop the country, with investors in banking and ICT sectors really keen to set up shop in one of the fastest growing economies in the region. After receiving the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019, there was greater social buy-in into Ahmed's leadership and vision, many expats who'd left their home country decades ago, were looking forward to returning home and rebuild the country. Ahmed appointed the country's first woman president, garnering more support as a new age African leader.
